trends.theme: Critical-minerals weaponisation — the binding constraint on the AI hardware build
trends.what_changed: China's expanded Oct 2025 rare-earth measures (0.1% extraterritorial rule) are suspended to Nov 2026, but seven REE controls stay live and the January 2026 Export Licensing Catalogue added rare-earth compounds, silver and more. IEA: gallium and heavy REE prices in Europe are ~5x Chinese domestic prices; full implementation would put $6.5tn/yr of non-China downstream production at risk.

evidence.src: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 — executive summary
CFR — Dismantling China's Supply-Chain Weapon

trends.theme: The AI capex flywheel is the portfolio's single largest tail risk
trends.what_changed: Hyperscaler 2026 AI capex raised to ~$730bn combined (+78% from ~$410bn in 2025), projected to reach $1.3tn in 2027. Nvidia market cap ~$5.3-5.8tn, FY26 revenue $215.9bn, $279bn in supply commitments, >$540bn of circular-financing deals. BofA's semiconductor Bubble Risk Indicator hit 0.91; the IMF and BIS have both flagged AI circular financing as systemic risk. Michael Burry disclosed sizable NVDA puts. Alphabet fell 7% in a single session after raising its own capex guidance; Meta fell on its report too.

trends.portfolio_action: NVDA is a watchlist name, not a core hold — correct call. The right structural question is not 'does AI end' but 'where does the money survive a digestion period'. Memory (MU), connectivity (MRVL, AVGO, ALAB) and power (GEV, NEE, CAT) survive a capex digestion; NVDA's multiple does not. Keep total AI-hardware exposure ≤40% of the portfolio.

trends.theme: The power capacity squeeze is now the bottleneck for AI itself
trends.what_changed: GE Vernova gas power equipment backlog and slot reservations climbed from 83 GW (end-2025) to 100 GW (Q1 2026) to 116 GW (Q2 2026), targeting 125 GW by year-end 2026. Only 53 GW is firm backlog; 63 GW is paid reservations. Total backlog $176bn. Lead times for a heavy-duty turbine now run to 2031; combined-cycle plant lead times have stretched from 3.5 years (2023) to ~5 years, and 7 for some frames. Output plan: 20 GW/yr from Q3 2026, 24 GW in 2028, 30 GW in 2030.

evidence.src: GE Vernova Q2 2026 results
Yahoo Finance — the gas turbine shortage just became AI's biggest constraint
Utility Dive — GE Vernova backlog climbs to 116 GW

losers: Data center developers without secured power
trends.portfolio_action: GEV is the single best expression of the AI-power bottleneck and is already on the monitor list with the strongest backtest numbers in the file (Sharpe 1.39, max drawdown -23%). Add it. CAT is the same trade with a $72.1bn backlog, +92% y/y, $42.5bn converting within 12 months.

trends.theme: Utilities are re-rating from yield plays to AI-infrastructure platforms
trends.what_changed: North American natural resources M&A hit a record $330.5bn in 1H26, with utility/power at ~70% of it. NextEra announced an all-stock $67bn acquisition of Dominion Energy (combined enterprise value ~$420bn), filed for regulatory approval July 15, 2026, expected to close 2H 2027. NextEra: 21 GW of hyperscaler opportunities in FPL's pipeline, ~12 GW in advanced negotiations; definitive US-Japan agreements to fund up to 10 GW of gas generation in Texas and Pennsylvania by end-2028; plans 15-30 GW of new capacity by 2035; Brookfield partnership to invest ~$100bn in an AI data center campus in Paducah, Kentucky.

evidence.src: Ion Analytics / Mergermarket — record North America natural resources M&A
PwC — Power and Utilities US Deals 2026 midyear outlook

Treat NEE as the power-sector anchor; if you want more upside, GEV or CAT gives the same exposure with a cleaner single-theme story.

trends.theme: Nuclear is back — 9.8 GW of hyperscaler commitments in 13 deals
trends.what_changed: Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft have signed for roughly 9.8 GW of nuclear output from operating, restarted and uprated US reactors; the IEA counts 45 GW of conditional agreements with SMR projects. First new capacity: Three Mile Island Unit 1's 835 MW restart (Microsoft, Constellation) targeted H2 2027. Amazon signed a 20-year PPA with Constellation for up to 690 MW from Calvert Cliffs (incl. a 190 MW uprate) plus a joint SMR exploration; Amazon also committed 12 Xe-100 SMRs at Cascade, WA. Meta up to 6.6 GW across TerraPower, Oklo, Vistra and Constellation targeting 2032-2035.

trends.theme: Behind-the-meter fuel cells: the shortest path to powering an AI campus
trends.what_changed: Bloom Energy: ~250 MW across nearly two dozen AI infrastructure customers, up from near zero two years ago. Equinix deployments across 19 data centers (>100 MW). Bloom is doubling manufacturing capacity from 1 GW to 2 GW annually by end-2026 (~$100m investment). Fuel cells can bring a data center online in ~90 days without grid connection.

trends.theme: US LNG: the structural shock absorber, growing ~20% by end-2027
trends.what_changed: US LNG exports averaged 17.4 Bcf/d in 1H26, +23% y/y, the fastest growth since large-scale exports began in 2016; EIA forecasts 18.7 Bcf/d in 1H27. Five export projects start up or ramp by end-2027 (Corpus Christi Stage 3, Golden Pass, Port Arthur Phase 1, Rio Grande LNG). When the Strait of Hormuz closed in March 2026 it cut off ~20% of global LNG trade, mostly Qatari, which doubled US shipments to Asia (+108%). JKM hit a four-year high of $15.56/MMBtu.

trends.theme: Space economy compounding at 11-17% — but growth is concentrated in orbital infrastructure, not launch
trends.what_changed: The global space economy was $556bn in 2025, $609bn in 2026, forecast $944bn by 2031 (11.2% CAGR). LEO is the fastest of the major orbit classes at 17.2% CAGR ($182bn to $403bn); broadband/connectivity 13.5% CAGR. Launch services are $22.7bn in 2026 (3.7% of the economy) growing at 14.8% CAGR to $41bn by 2031 — faster than the headline but still a small slice, and SpaceX holds ~87% of global upmass with reusable heavy-lift capturing >70% of upmass-weighted launch revenue. Allianz: LEO services go from ~$16bn (2025) to ~$120bn (2030), a 7-8x expansion, inside a space economy tripling to $1.8tn+ by 2035.

evidence.src: HiQual Insights — Space Economy: LEO Constellations & Launch Market 2026-2031
Allianz Research — Low earth, high stakes, July 2026
OECD — The Space Economy at a Glance 2026

trends.portfolio_action: The space theme is intact but the launch sub-segment is a smaller share of it than the narrative implies. Do not size RKLB as if launch is the whole space economy.

trends.theme: Rocket Lab: the thesis is intact, the catalyst just moved a year
trends.what_changed: On Oct 14, 2026 Rocket Lab confirmed Neutron's first flight has slipped to 2027 (fourth slip since 2021) due to a carbon-composite forward-dome manufacturing defect. Stock fell 7.9% on the day, another ~7.3% after hours, and 6.6% the next session; it is ~63% below its May 27, 2026 all-time high of $151, closing near $52-53. Underlying fundamentals are unchanged and strong: Q2 2026 revenue $234m (+62% y/y), $437m+ in new launch contracts, total backlog $2.2-2.4bn, 90+ launches, a $397m Space Force SB-AMTI contract, $160m+ across two GEO satellite builds, and a Kepler dedicated Neutron mission for 2028. CFO: cash-flow positivity is a function of Neutron's first successful launch and could take 18-24 months after that.

evidence.src: Yahoo Finance — Rocket Lab shares slide 15% as Neutron launch delayed until 2027
TheStreet — tiny air pockets stall Rocket Lab's answer to SpaceX
SEC filing — Rocket Lab Q2 2026 results (revenue $234m, $437m new launch contracts)

losers: Any position sized to a 2026 Neutron flight
trends.portfolio_action: This is the clearest buy-the-delay opportunity in the portfolio: the backlog, the Space Force award and the commercial bookings are real and unchanged; only the flight date moved. But it is a $33-35bn market cap against $769m trailing revenue (~41-54x sales) on a GAAP loss, so size it as the small, high-volatility conviction position it already is. Do NOT add to RKLB here — the pending 258-share order at $58.06 is already above the current ~$52-53 price; let it fill, then hold. Wait for a successful Neutron flight plus 18-24 months of cash-flow commentary before sizing up.

trends.theme: Rates are going UP, not down — the Fed has re-entered a hiking cycle
trends.what_changed: The FOMC unanimously raised the fed funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% at its Sept 15-16, 2026 meeting — the first increase since July 2023. The September minutes (released Oct 7) show officials 'overwhelmingly' concluded more work was needed; 16 of 18 policymakers expected at least one more quarter-point move by year-end, and most wanted rates at or above that level throughout 2027. Fed staff projected inflation reaching 2% only in 2029. October hike odds have swung from ~70% to ~23% on Jefferson and Williams pushing back, but U.S. Bank now expects a cumulative 75bp of increases between September 2026 and March 2027, peaking at 4.25-4.50%.

evidence.src: NYT — Fed minutes show officials saw more work to do to quell inflation
ANI — Fed minutes signal another hike likely by year-end
U.S. Bank October 2026 Economic Outlook — 75bp cumulative tightening to 4.25-4.50%

trends.portfolio_action: This is the most important macro fact for the portfolio and it argues for reducing unprofitable-growth exposure. The Sharesies holdings in QBTS (-33% in 6 months), RGTI (-35%), IREN (-36%) and DTIL (-35%) are exactly the names that get de-rated by a hiking Fed. If you are not adding to them, they are a slow leak. Harvest them into the power and memory names that are earning through the cycle.

trends.theme: Inflation is supply-shock driven and the Fed cannot fix it
trends.what_changed: The IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook (released Oct 13 in Bangkok) puts global growth at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, with inflation reaching 4.7% this year on higher energy and food prices, and flags that 'the margins of adjustment that made the global economy resilient are rapidly narrowing'. IMF estimates a ~30% probability US growth falls below 1% in 2027 (a mild recession starting Q4 2026) and a ~30% probability US headline inflation exceeds 4% in 2027. Fed staff see 2% inflation only in 2029. US CPI has now been above 2% for the longest stretch of the 21st century, and economists warn the Fed risking recession by hiking into a supply shock.

evidence.src: IMF WEO press briefing, Bangkok, Oct 13 2026
IMF — Global Economic Resilience Is Under Strain
CNBC — rate-hike odds rising after CPI; recession risk debate

trends.portfolio_action: The inflation regime argues for a real-asset sleeve. Gold has already pulled back ~25% from its late-January 2026 record (spot ~$4,188 on Oct 13) with central banks buying 289 tonnes in Q2 2026 (+62% y/y) — J.P. Morgan still sees $6,000/oz by Q4 2026. On Sharesies, Smartshares GLD (NZX, PIE-taxed, 0.55% TER) or ASX GDX are the clean ways to add a 3-5% gold allocation. This is the single highest-conviction addition in this brief.

trends.theme: China's 15th Five-Year Plan doubles down on technology self-sufficiency, not consumption
trends.what_changed: The 15th FYP (2026-2030), adopted at the Fourth Plenum on Oct 23, 2025 and ratified at the March 2026 NPC, sets a 2026 GDP target of 4.5-5% (down from ~5%) and includes a binding target to raise total energy production capacity by more than 20%. R&D spending to grow at least 7% annually (~40% cumulative). The value-added of 'core digital economy industries' to reach 12.5% of GDP. Critically, the household-consumption objective remains secondary with no binding figures or timetable.

evidence.src: BNP Paribas — China's 15th Five-Year Plan: prioritising power over addressing imbalances
European Parliament EPRS briefing on the 15th FYP
KPMG — Key Takeaways from China's 2026 Two Sessions

beneficiaries: Domestic Chinese tech (not in this portfolio)
losers: New Zealand and Australian exporters levered to Chinese consumption (dairy, tourism)
trends.portfolio_action: This is the main reason to be cautious about AIR (Air New Zealand) and other China-levered consumer exports. New Zealand's China-bound goods ran at nearly double the next two export markets combined, so a plan that suppresses Chinese household consumption is a headwind to NZ export income.

trends.theme: New Zealand: the RBNZ is hiking too, and oil is the transmission mechanism
trends.what_changed: The RBNZ raised the OCR 25bp to 2.75% on Sept 2, 2026 with inflation at 4.1% driven by Middle East fuel prices, and signalled another increase could follow by year-end. Chief Economist Paul Conway said on Oct 15 the late-October decision is 'completely open' between a hold and a 25bp hike. ASB expects 25bp hikes at both the October and December meetings to a 3.25% end-2026 OCR; Westpac expects a pause in October and a hike in December, with a 4% peak in 2027 and a 4.25% peak held through 2028 before returning to neutral in 2029.

evidence.src: Pound Sterling Live — RBNZ's Conway keeps the hike alive (ASB: 3.25% end-2026 OCR)
Westpac — RBNZ MPS review, Sept 2 2026
ANZ — RBNZ MPR review, July 8 2026

trends.portfolio_action: The NZ-listed holdings in the Sharesies portfolio (AIR, CO2, PEB, USH) are the most exposed to a hiking RBNZ. Prefer NZD-hedged or US-listed growth exposure while the OCR is rising — the existing US-heavy allocation is correctly positioned.
